text.en: Anton Chekhov's comic play shows a man who has come to propose, but ends up quarrelling.

The Proposal is a one-act play by Anton Chekhov, written in 1888-89.
The three characters are Stepan Chubukov, a landowner, his twenty-five-year-old daughter Natalya, and their neighbour Ivan Lomov.
Lomov comes in a dress-jacket and white gloves to ask for Natalya's hand. He is hearty but very suspicious.
Before he can ask, he begins to quarrel with Natalya about who owns a piece of land called Oxen Meadows.
They then argue about whose dog is better, and each calls the other names. Chubukov joins the quarrel.
In the end the proposal is made and accepted, though the quarrelling goes on.
The play is a farce that shows the tendency of wealthy families to arrange marriages that make economic sense.
It teaches how small matters of pride and property can ruin a serious moment, and humour makes us see it.

points.en: The Proposal is a comic play by Chekhov.
Lomov comes to propose but quarrels.
Oxen Meadows and dogs cause arguments.
It shows petty quarrels and economic marriage.
